title: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama says new-look 'shunk' done because of blister on hand
author: Hana
summary: Not every story this week was about the scoreboard—sometimes it's about a blister on a 7-foot-4 phenom's hand that led to the invention of the "shunk."

content.value:
## Not every story this week was about the scoreboard.

ESPN (Michael Wright) reported: **"Spurs' Victor Wembanyama says new-look 'shunk' done because of blister on hand"**

Box scores don't capture all of it. They never do, really. The numbers will tell you about Victor Wembanyama's points and blocks and all the ways he warps a basketball game just by being on the floor. But they won't tell you about the blister. They won't tell you that the reason he's been throwing the ball down differently lately—that soft, controlled finish everyone's been calling the "shunk"—came down to something as small and human as damaged skin on his palm. It's the kind of detail that reminds you these aren't just highlight reels in sneakers. They're people, dealing with the same annoying little injuries the rest of us would slap a Band-Aid on and complain about. Except when you're seven-foot-four and your job is to dunk a basketball, a blister becomes a storyline. This is the part that usually gets left out, and honestly, it's often the part worth remembering.
